step_by_step_reasoning: 1) The whiteboard shows a fire hydrant (IoT edge device), API Gateway, S3, ECS, SageMaker and an Analyst. 2) Transcript: smart fire hydrants record acoustic signals daily and push correlated files through API Gateway (authentication/security layer), which persists them in S3. 3) A daily batch process in ECS processes the files as node pairs to find correlations and persistent correlations (processor-intensive, hence containers instead of Lambda). 4) ECS sends persistent correlations to a SageMaker ML endpoint that assigns a leak probability score. 5) The score is fed to the human analyst team, who qualify the leak and update its status to field investigation required. 6) Field feedback about every six weeks is used to retrain the model (feedback loop from analyst to SageMaker). The analyst is kept because it is an explicitly drawn actor participating in the scoring and retraining flows. No additional components were invented.

graph.name: Mueller Water Products - Water Intelligence Platform (Acoustic Leak Detection)
graph.notes: Water intelligence platform that ingests daily acoustic data from smart fire hydrants through API Gateway into S3, runs daily batch correlation processing on ECS, classifies persistent correlations with a SageMaker ML endpoint to produce a leak probability, and feeds the score to human analysts. Field feedback is used roughly every six weeks to retrain the model. Benefits: reduced non-revenue water loss and ecological protection.

nodes.name: Smart Fire Hydrant
nodes.notes: IoT edge devices (smart fire hydrants) in a large-scale IoT network. Record acoustic signals daily that measure noises on the pipe network; signals are correlated between multiple fire hydrants.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Ingestion entry point for the daily acoustic files. Provides authentication and security; chosen over direct S3 upload because of the heavy focus on IoT security.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Persists the acoustic signal files pushed through API Gateway.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Daily batch process on container microservices. Processes each file as a node pair to find correlations in the acoustic signals, including persistent correlations occurring over many days. Chosen over Lambda because the acoustic algorithms are very processor intensive.

nodes.name: SageMaker ML Endpoint
nodes.notes: ML endpoint that classifies persistent correlations and assigns a leak probability (leak score). Model is retrained about every six weeks using feedback from the field.

nodes.name: Analyst
nodes.notes: Human analyst team that receives the leak score, reviews the persistent correlation, talks with the water utility to rule out other nearby noise sources, and updates the leak status to field investigation required. Field feedback is used to retrain the model.

edges.notes: Correlated acoustic signal files are pushed through API Gateway on a daily basis.
After authentication and security checks, the files are pushed and persisted in S3.
Daily batch process in ECS processes each file as a node pair to look for correlations in the acoustic signals.
Persistent correlations are sent to the SageMaker ML endpoint for further classification and probability assignment.
Leak score (probability) is fed to the human analyst team for further classification of the leak.
Feedback from the field is used about every six weeks to further classify and retrain the model so it improves over time.
